package verify

// The must-trip fixture for the undeclared arm: a persisted struct carrying a
// text field the registry never declared.
//
// `stderr` is in the vocabulary and the field is a string, so it matches. What
// makes it a fault is that nothing says where the value comes from — a new sink
// added to a schema with no disposition is exactly the gap the registry exists
// to close, and it must fail rather than pass by not being noticed.
type ToolRun struct {
	Tool   string `json:"tool"`
	Stderr string `json:"stderr,omitempty"`
}

// The must-NOT-trip sibling: a text-shaped field whose tag is outside the
// vocabulary. A prefix-matching regression would report this one, silently
// widening the guard past what the registry can answer for.
type Annotation struct {
	Footnote string `json:"footnote,omitempty"`
	Slug     string `json:"slug"`
	Count    int    `json:"notes"`
}

// The []string arm: a slice-of-string sink is a sink. Restricting the walk to
// scalar strings would miss verify.Scope.Degraded entirely.
type Degradation struct {
	Degraded []string `json:"degraded,omitempty"`
}
